comments.body:
RUNTIME VERIFICATION COMPLETE — ALL THREE ARMS GREEN on a live run, which is the one thing the
implementation could not evidence for itself.

RUN 30846201728, head d4095763e (VERIFIED to contain the [llm] model fix before reading any result):
    success   external LLM (live anthropic)
    success   external LLM (live openai)
    success   external LLM (live bedrock)
    success   external integration (live services)
    success   langfuse tracing round-trip (ephemeral self-hosted)
So the matrix runs one arm per credentialed provider, all three execute against real providers, and all
three pass. AC1/AC2 are now demonstrated at runtime rather than only statically.

THE ROUTE HERE MATTERED, AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT WAS A FALSE NEGATIVE WORTH RECORDING.
Run 30836378745 (pre-fix) failed the bedrock and openai arms. Run 30843695520 failed them IDENTICALLY —
and I nearly read that as the fix not working. It was not: that runs head was f2b2d0b41, which I
verified does NOT contain the fix. Gerrit merged at 18:58:32 and the dispatch was 18:58:47, before the
GitHub MIRROR replicated, so Actions checked out main as GitHub knew it — pre-fix code. The lesson is
concrete: after a Gerrit submit, a CI dispatch must wait for mirror replication, and an arm result must
never be read without first asserting the runs head SHA carries the change. Both watchers now do that.

WHAT THE PRE-FIX FAILURES PROVED, which is the storys actual point: the arms failed LOUDLY rather than
skipping to green. The bedrock arm reported `[llm-live-canary] collected=14 executed=14 skipped=0` with
11 tests making real Bedrock calls and passing. A vacuous green was impossible — which is exactly the
failure mode AC4 exists to prevent, demonstrated by a real red rather than argued.

THE DEFECT THE LIVE RUN FOUND, now fixed (Gerrit 1308): the overlays set only [llm.model_classes], but
cfg.model is a SECOND resolution path the class table cannot reach — config.py:575 falls back to
DEFAULT_MODEL, the bare literal "claude-opus-4-8", which infers provider anthropic. Three tests read
cfg.model rather than naming a class and so called direct Anthropic on EVERY arm, failing with "Could not
resolve authentication method" because non-Anthropic arms deliberately blank ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

AND THIS STORYS OWN GUARD HAD THE SAME BLIND SPOT — worth recording as a design lesson, not just a bug:
`test_every_model_class_resolves_to_the_declared_provider` PASSED on all three arms while those arms
called Anthropic, because it only checks the three CLASS names and never cfg.model. Its docstring claims
to catch "a partial overlay would leave some ops on the default provider, which is the ambient default
this story removes" — so the assertion was over the WRONG SURFACE for the storys stated goal. Added
`test_the_ambient_default_model_also_resolves_to_the_declared_provider`, which asserts
LLMConfig.from_env().model is provider-qualified.
WORSE, A TEST WAS ENFORCING THE BUG: `test_each_overlay_sets_only_the_model_classes_table` asserted
set(data["llm"]) == {"model_classes"}, so the fix could not land without that test failing
(`Extra items in the left set: model`). Its module docstring encoded the same assumption. It now pins
BOTH selection keys and still forbids unrelated ones, which was its real intent. A test that pins the
wrong surface is worse than no test, because it certifies the gap.

ALSO FIXED: review_skeleton.yamls model_ladder was three literal claude-* ids, which pinned an Anthropic
ladder into any providers run; now [trivial, standard, frontier]. No bare ladder id remains under
workflow/. test_review_kernel_rules_live needed NO change — its docstring already claimed the overlay
repoints it, which was false before the fix and is true after.

VERIFIED TOKEN-FREE that the overlay now repoints the ambient default per arm:
    anthropic -> cfg.model=anthropic:claude-opus-4-8
    bedrock   -> cfg.model=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    openai    -> cfg.model=openai:gpt-5.4

OPERATOR ACTIONS THAT UNBLOCKED THIS, recorded so the sequence is reconstructable: the OpenAI arm was
previously 429 insufficient_quota (the key AUTHENTICATED — 429 not 401 — and OpenAI echoed model_name
back, so the ids were always real and entitled); a funded key was set as the OPENAI_API_KEY repository
secret. The IAM role rebar-external-ci-bedrock was created with trust scoped to
repository=navapbc/rebar and sub EXACTLY repo:navapbc/rebar:ref:refs/heads/main (StringEquals, no glob),
permissions limited to bedrock:InvokeModel* on anthropic.claude-*, no managed policies. Role assumption
and region resolution both confirmed in-run.

STILL TO CONFIRM FROM THE LOGS once the run fully completes (the jira DC job is still going and GitHub
serves no logs until then): each arms `[llm-live-canary] executed=N` figure, so a green is recorded as
genuinely-executed rather than inferred from a job conclusion.

compiled_state.description:
# S10 — external integration tests cover MULTIPLE live providers

## Context / Problem

The external integration suite is the only place rebar exercises a REAL provider end to end, and it
runs on ONE provider. `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` gates every live job on
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (lines 46, 124, 185, 247; the `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback appears only in the guard
message, not as a matrix arm), and `prompt-eval.yml` likewise. So the provider seam this epic built —
first-class Anthropic AND Bedrock, best-effort OpenAI-compatible — has exactly one arm under live test.
A Bedrock-only regression (throttling shape, a `cachePoint` envelope change, an inference-profile id
that stops resolving, structured output degrading) cannot be caught by CI today. It can only be caught
by a human running the gates locally, which is what S7b makes possible and is NOT a substitute for
automation.

This is the THIRD of the three permanent provider switches, the other two being the repo config / local
environment [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] and the AWS review bot [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a]. It is
deliberately NOT "flip CI to Bedrock": the goal is live-grounded confidence across every provider we
hold credentials for, so a MATRIX, not a switch. Flipping the single arm from Anthropic to Bedrock would
trade one blind spot for another.

## Approach

Make provider a MATRIX DIMENSION of the external suite rather than an ambient default. Run the live jobs
once per credentialed provider — Anthropic, Bedrock, and OpenAI where a key exists — and have each arm
SKIP LOUDLY when its credential is absent, so a missing secret is visible as a skip rather than
indistinguishable from a green run.

SELECT THE PROVIDER THROUGH `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`, the layered config-file pointer, rather than
bespoke per-arm CI wiring. Each matrix arm writes a small config file setting only
`[llm.model_classes]` and points the env var at it. This is the right instrument for three reasons:
it is the mechanism rebar already documents for exactly this purpose (`docs/local-dev-env.md`, landed by
S7b), it DEEP-MERGES over the discovered config instead of replacing it so the arm overrides provider
and model and nothing else, and it means CI DOGFOODS the same override path a developer uses — so the
pointer itself gets live coverage on every run instead of being exercised only by hand. The deprecated
bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` is explicitly not the instrument: it cannot express per-class models.

Bedrock authenticates from the AWS credential chain, not an API key, so the matrix cannot key on "an API
key secret exists"; the Bedrock arm needs its own credential presence check.

THE S7 PRECEDENT DOES NOT TRANSFER, and an earlier draft of this plan wrongly said it did. S7
[rebar:9249-1569-7be9-4f67] grants an EC2 INSTANCE ROLE reached via IMDS from inside
`compose-review-bot-1` (caller identity `assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/<instance-id>`). The
external suite runs on `ubuntu-latest` (`external-integration.yml:32`) — a GitHub-hosted runner with no
instance role and no IMDS path to that host. So the CI arm needs its OWN credential mechanism, named
explicitly: OIDC federation — `permissions: id-token: write` plus
`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` assuming a dedicated, scoped Bedrock role modelled on S7's
POLICY (reuse the policy shape, not the delivery path). Static long-lived keys in a secret are the
rejected alternative: they would put a durable AWS credential in CI to save a one-time role setup.

REGION MUST BE SET EXPLICITLY, and the `[llm.model_classes]` file cannot carry it. Bug [rebar:a574]
established by measurement that IMDS does NOT supply a region and that Bedrock hard-fails with
`NoRegionError` at client construction when none resolves — and that rebar's own
`REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` alone was insufficient, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` was also required. The Bedrock
arm therefore sets BOTH as job env. This is a real trap, not a hypothetical: it already broke a Bedrock
cutover once.

Cost is the real constraint: N providers multiplies the live spend of a suite that already runs weekly.
Decide and record whether every provider runs on every trigger, or whether non-default providers run on
a reduced cadence or a reduced case subset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The external suite runs its live jobs for MORE THAN ONE provider, with provider as an explicit
      matrix dimension rather than an ambient default read from whichever key happens to be set.
- [ ] Anthropic and Bedrock are both covered. OpenAI is covered where a credential exists, or its
      absence is recorded as a deliberate decision with the reason.
- [ ] Each arm selects its provider via `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` pointing at a config file that sets
      ONLY `[llm.model_classes]`, NOT via the deprecated bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL`. A test or CI assertion
      pins that the override changes provider/model and leaves the rest of the discovered config intact.
- [ ] An arm whose credential is ABSENT skips LOUDLY and is distinguishable in the run output from an arm
      that ran and passed — a missing secret must never read as green.
- [ ] The Bedrock arm obtains credentials by a NAMED mechanism valid on a GitHub-hosted runner — OIDC
      role assumption via `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` to a dedicated scoped role (the S7 EC2
      instance-role path is NOT reachable from `ubuntu-latest`) — and a test or CI assertion pins that it
      does not silently fall back to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- [ ] The Bedrock arm resolves an AWS region explicitly, setting BOTH `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` and
      `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` as job env, and FAILS LOUDLY with the typed configuration error (per
      [rebar:a574]) when no region resolves — it must never skip silently or read as green.
- [ ] The per-trigger COST of the matrix is measured and recorded, and the cadence decision (every
      trigger vs reduced cadence/subset per provider) is stated with its rationale.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green; the config-read
      and env-drift gates pass.
compiled_state.title: S10 — external integration tests cover MULTIPLE live providers, not just Anthropic
